title: Heavy-Tailed Memory Traces in Long-Horizon Language Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.00010v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-horizon language agents increasingly rely on external memory as a frozen world model, yet current memory systems are usually judged only by task success or token cost. We argue that the missing object is the shape of memory use: under finite context and repeated retrieval, agent memory can concentrate on a small core while leaving rare states in a long tail where prediction errors accumulate. We study this effect through a conservative tail audit and find that concentration is reproducible but policy-dependent. Random-walk agents produce log-normal-compatible retrieval artifacts, whereas semantic LLM policies yield the strongest truncated-power-law-compatible core--tail traces. Motivated by this audit, we propose Core--Tail World Model (CTWM), a rank-based memory controller that allocates prompt budget with a single exponent $\tau$ while retaining a summarized tail. On Synthetic Graph World, CTWM preserves full state and transition

translated_title: 长程语言智能体中的重尾记忆痕迹
translated_abstract: 长程语言智能体越来越依赖外部记忆作为冻结的世界模型，然而当前的记忆系统通常仅以任务成功率或令牌成本来评价。我们认为，缺失的考察对象是记忆使用的形态：在有限上下文与重复检索的条件下，智能体记忆可能集中于一个小的核心，而将稀有状态留在长尾部分，预测误差会在长尾中不断累积。我们通过一种保守的尾部审计方法研究了这一效应，发现记忆集中现象是可复现的，但依赖于具体策略：随机游走智能体产生的检索痕迹符合对数正态分布，而语义化的LLM策略则产生最强的符合截断幂律的核心-尾部痕迹。受此审计启发，我们提出了核心-尾部世界模型，这是一种基于排名的记忆控制器，它使用单一指数τ来分配提示预算，同时保留一个摘要化的尾部。在合成图世界（Synthetic Graph World）上，CTWM能够保留完整的状态与转移信息。
tldr: 该论文发现长程语言智能体的记忆使用呈现“核心集中、长尾积累预测误差”的重尾形态，并提出基于单一指数τ分配提示预算、同时保留摘要化尾部的核心-尾部世界模型（CTWM）记忆控制器。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals that long-horizon language agents exhibit heavy-tailed, core–tail memory traces—where prediction errors accumulate in rare tail states—and proposes CTWM, a rank-based memory controller that allocates prompt budget with a single exponent τ while retaining a summarized tail.
